record.paper_title: QM2017: Status and Key open Questions in Ultra-Relativistic Heavy-Ion Physics
record.original_question: What are the relevant microscopic degrees of freedom in the strongly interacting quark-gluon plasma if they are not quasi-free quarks and gluons, and how can precision measurements of macroscopic properties and transport coefficients identify them?

evidence.quote: We have measured with increasing precision its macroscopic properties and many transport coefficients (EOS, cS, η/S, ξ/S, D, q̂, ê); we have good evidence for deconfinement from J/ψ regeneration (colour conductivity) and sequential Υ suppression (resonance melting); we have some indirect evidence for chiral symmetry restoration (ρ melting, strangeness enhancement).
And we also learned that the d.o.f. of the Quark-Gluon Plasma are definitely not (quasi-free) quarks and gluons.
On a deeper level, much also remains to be discovered: Primarily, what are actually the relevant degrees of freedom?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
In ultra-relativistic heavy-ion collisions a strongly interacting deconfined state of QCD matter — the quark–gluon plasma (QGP) — is produced at temperatures above the QCD pseudocritical temperature T_c ≈ 155 MeV. Phenomenology shows that the QGP behaves as a near-perfect fluid with very small specific shear viscosity η/s, and a variety of macroscopic properties and transport coefficients have been measured or inferred, including the equation of state p(ε), the speed of sound c_S, the shear and bulk viscosities η/s and ζ/s, the heavy-quark spatial diffusion coefficient D_s, the jet transport parameter q̂, and the parton energy-loss coefficient ê. There is also evidence for deconfinement (J/ψ regeneration, sequential Υ suppression) and indirect signs of chiral symmetry restoration (ρ-meson modification, strangeness enhancement). These observations are inconsistent with a description in terms of quasi-free quarks and gluons.

Problem. Identify the relevant microscopic degrees of freedom of the strongly coupled QGP at temperatures in the regime roughly T_c ≲ T ≲ a few × T_c. Concretely:

(a) Propose a set of effective constituents (e.g., dressed quasiparticles, hadron-like bound states, semi-classical color fields, holographic/AdS-CFT-inspired excitations, or other) and a corresponding effective theory or kinetic/transport framework that simultaneously reproduces the measured equation of state and speed of sound (including lattice-QCD results), the small η/s near the KSS bound 1/(4π), the bulk viscosity ζ/s peak near T_c, and the heavy-quark and jet transport coefficients D_s, q̂, ê.

(b) Determine which combinations of precision measurements of these macroscopic properties and transport coefficients can discriminate between competing candidate sets of degrees of freedom, and exhibit observables (with quantitative predictions) whose values uniquely fix the microscopic content of the medium.
artifact.status_search_result: The identification of the microscopic degrees of freedom of the strongly coupled quark–gluon plasma remains a central open question in high-energy nuclear physics. Subsequent reviews and white papers (e.g., the long-range plans for nuclear physics and EIC/sPHENIX/LHC heavy-ion programs) continue to list this as a key unresolved issue, with no consensus identification of the constituents.
